title: 1996 AHSME Problem 13
statement: Sunny runs at a steady rate, and Moonbeam runs \(m\) times as fast, where \(m\) is a number greater than \(1.\) If Moonbeam gives Sunny a head start of \(h\) meters, how many meters must Moonbeam run to overtake Sunny?

solutions.text: Suppose Moonbeam runs \(x\) meters. The elapsed time is \(\frac{x}{mv},\) so Sunny runs \(\frac{v\cdot x}{mv}=\frac{x}{m}\) meters after the start. At the catch, \(x=h+\frac{x}{m}.\) Solving gives \(x=\frac{hm}{m-1},\) so the correct answer is D.
hints: Let Sunny’s speed be \(v\) and Moonbeam’s speed be \(mv\)
If Moonbeam runs \(x\) meters, express Sunny’s distance during the same time in terms of \(x\)
